Data-quality diagnostics for DHS recode files

Source: R/quality.R
bdhs_quality.Rd

Computes the standard DHS data-quality indicators (the "Data quality tables" of the final report appendices and the DHS Methodological Reports on data quality) for whichever recode file is supplied. Each check uses the variables it needs and is skipped, with a message, when they are absent, so the same call works on PR, KR, BR and IR files.

Usage

bdhs_quality(
  data,
  checks = NULL,
  survey = NULL,
  population = c("de_facto", "de_jure", "all"),
  vars = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A recode data frame from bdhs_read() (numeric codes, not factors), or pooled data from bdhs_pool().

checks

Checks to run (see Details); NULL runs all those the data support.

survey

Optional survey reference when data does not carry one.

population

For household members (PR): "de_facto" (default, hv103 == 1), "de_jure" (hv102 == 1) or "all".

vars

Variables for the "completeness" check; NULL uses a default list of key variables, keeping those present.

Value

A tibble of class bdhs_quality with columns survey_id, recode, check, statistic, group (sex, year, variable, ...), value, benchmark (the value expected with good data), interpretation and n (number of cases behind the value). The attribute profiles holds the single-year age distribution (age) and births by calendar year (births), drawn by plot().

Details

The checks are:

  • "age_heaping" (PR, hv105, hv104): Whipple's index (ages 23-62, terminal digits 0 and 5; 100 = no preference, 500 = every age ends in 0 or 5) and Myers' blended index (ages 10-89; 0 = no preference, 90 = every age ends in the same digit), for both sexes and by sex, and the share of members with age missing or "don't know". The single-year age distribution is kept for plot().

  • "age_displacement" (PR): ratios of the numbers aged 14 to 15, 50 to 49 and 50 to 51 (men also 55 to 54). Interviewers who move women out of the eligible age range (15-49) inflate the counts at 14 and 50; values near 1 are expected. A high 50/49 ratio with an equally high 50/51 ratio points to heaping on 50 rather than displacement.

  • "birth_date_completeness" (BR, KR, or IR birth history, b10): percentage of births with month and year of birth reported (b10 codes 0 "month, year and day" and 1 "month and year", the same in every BDHS round), overall, for living and dead children and for births in the last 5 and 15 years, plus the percentage of living children whose birth date (hence age) was partly imputed.

  • "births_by_year" (b3, v008): births by calendar year and the calendar-year ratio \(100 B_x / ((B_{x-1} + B_{x+1}) / 2)\), also by completed years before the interview. A ratio well below 100 just inside the five-year window (calendar year interview year - 5, or 4 years before the interview) together with one above 100 just outside it suggests births were displaced out of the window that triggers the health questions. KR files only hold births of the last 5 years (3 in 1993-94), so only interior years are available; births_year4_vs_year3 (births 48-59 vs 36-47 months before the interview) then gives a window-edge check.

  • "age_at_death" (b6, b7): share of deaths with age at death reported in days, months and years, or missing, and the heaping index at 12 months, \(100 D_{12} / ((D_{11} + D_{13}) / 2)\), where \(D_{12}\) counts deaths reported at 12 months or "1 year" (and the same index from the imputed months in b7).

  • "anthropometry": for children (PR hc*, KR/BR hw*) and for women (ha*) and men (hb*) in PR: percentage with weight or height missing, percentage of z-scores flagged by DHS (codes 9996-9998), percentage of the remaining z-scores outside the WHO plausible limits (height-for-age -6 to 6, weight-for-age -6 to 5, weight-for-height -5 to 5), mean and standard deviation of the valid z-scores (WHO expects an SD of about 1.0-1.2; larger values point to measurement error), and digit preference of the terminal (decimal) digit of weight and height: percentage ending in 0, in 0 or 5 (expected 20) and the index of dissimilarity from a uniform digit distribution (0 = none, 90 = all on one digit).

  • "completeness": percentage missing (NA) and percentage coded as "don't know", "missing" or "inconsistent" (read from the value labels) for key variables (vars). NA includes rows skipped by design (for example m14 for births outside the reference period).

All statistics are unweighted, as in the DHS data-quality tables. For PR files the household population is the de facto population (hv103 == 1) by default.

References

Pullum, T. W. (2006). An assessment of age and date reporting in the DHS surveys, 1985-2003. DHS Methodological Reports No. 5.

Pullum, T. W. and Staveteig, S. (2017). An assessment of the quality and consistency of age and date reporting in DHS surveys, 2000-2015. DHS Methodological Reports No. 19.

See also

plot.bdhs_quality()

Examples

pr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "PR")
q <- bdhs_quality(pr, checks = c("age_heaping", "anthropometry"))
q[q$statistic %in% c("whipple", "myers"), c("statistic", "group", "value")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   statistic group   value
#>   <chr>     <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 whipple   total  101.  
#> 2 myers     total    3.70
#> 3 whipple   male   105.  
#> 4 myers     male     4.06
#> 5 whipple   female  96.4 
#> 6 myers     female   4.01
br <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "BR")
bdhs_quality(br, checks = "births_by_year")
#> # A tibble: 41 × 9
#>    survey_id recode check   statistic group value benchmark interpretation     n
#>    <chr>     <chr>  <chr>   <chr>     <chr> <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>          <dbl>

#>  2 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2002   93.4       100 NA                64
#>  3 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2003   93.2       100 NA                69
#>  4 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2004  120         100 excess            84
#>  5 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2005   82.1       100 deficit           71
#>  6 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2006  115.        100 excess            89
#>  7 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2007   98.8       100 NA                84
#>  8 BD2022DHS BR     births… calendar… 2008   93.1       100 NA                81
